slides.0.title: Terroir in depth
slides.0.subtitle: The Danube, the Pannonian plain and soils
slides.1.title: Danube terroir: gneiss and loess
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Wachau's division of labour
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Riesling tends to sit on the upper terraces of gneiss, amphibolite and quartzite, Grüner Veltliner on the lower loess
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Cool nights and the valley
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The valley lets cold Alpine air meet warm days, giving diurnal range that keeps acidity and aroma
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Wagram's loess
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wagram is known for loess terrain, closely tied to Grüner Veltliner
slides.1.content: Gneiss tends to mineral tension, loess to roundness and pepper; this is a general stylistic contrast.
slides.2.title: Pannonian terroir: lake and limestone
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The lake effect
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The shallow steppe Neusiedler See produces autumn mist and humidity that promote noble rot
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Leithaberg
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner; reds at least 85% Blaufränkisch (limestone and schist soils are general knowledge, not individually checked)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Steiermark's cool, wet climate
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Rainfall up to about 800 mm, wetter than the east, favouring aromatic whites
slides.2.content: In an essay, start with climate (continental/Pannonian), then soils and varieties.
In Wachau, which soil is Grüner Veltliner mostly planted on?
Grüner Veltliner is mostly on lower loess and Riesling on gneiss.
What is Neusiedler See's main contribution to sweet wines?
B. Autumn mist and humidity promoting noble rot
The lake's humidity and autumn mist make noble rot likely.
What is the main rule for Leithaberg DAC reds?
Leithaberg reds are at least 85% Blaufränkisch.
